security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU TCG implements the SMIP trap entry/exit sequence with the pre-PR ordering (cspspush/cspspop at the old positions). On trap entry, saving x10-x15 after cspspush means registers land on the handler stack instead of the interrupted context's stack, corrupting the handler stack. On trap exit, restoring x10-x15 before cspspop means registers are loaded from the handler stack instead of the interrupted context's stack, leaking or corrupting context state.
security_spec.summary: SMIP reorders cspspush/cspspop relative to register save/restore in trap entry/exit; QEMU TCG using the old ordering corrupts handler stack on entry and leaks interrupted-context state on exit

findings.finding: SMIP trap-entry stack-pointer swap (SP↔XSP) is NOT implemented. This code only clears ELP per Zicfilp. The vulnerability pattern 'cspspush before save x10-x15' cannot manifest because cspspush/cspspop do not exist in this codebase.

SRET return path does not contain SMIP SP↔XSP swap logic. Only Zicfilp ELP restore is present. The vulnerability pattern 'cspspop before restore x10-x15' cannot be triggered because SMIP is not implemented.
MRET return path does not contain SMIP SP↔XSP swap logic. Only Zicfilp ELP restore is present. The vulnerability pattern cannot be triggered because SMIP is not implemented.
No XSP (alternate stack pointer) field exists in CPURISCVState. The struct contains ssp (Zicfiss) and elp (Zicfilp) but no SMIP state. No data-corruption vector exists without SMIP state.

MENVCFG write-path validates Zicfilp LPE and Zicfiss SSE bits but has no SMIP enablement bit. The mask correctly guards only implemented extensions. No SMIP vulnerability can arise from MENVCFG writes.
CSR SSP (Zicfiss shadow-stack pointer) accessors exist but no XSP CSR handlers exist. SMIP has no CSR footprint in this codebase, so no CSR read/write vulnerabilities are possible.
Only ext_zicfilp and ext_zicfiss CFI extension flags are declared. No ext_smip flag exists. Without an enable flag, SMIP cannot be activated, so no vulnerability path exists.

Extension validation covers existing CFI extensions (Zicfiss, Zicfilp) with correct dependency chains. No SMIP validation exists because the extension is not implemented. No misconfiguration vector exists.
Backward-CFI enablement helper gates only Zicfiss SSE bits. SMIP has no enablement check here because it is not implemented. No privilege-escalation or bypass vector exists via this path.
